page: Microsoft Azure D128ls_v6 is a low-memory variant within the general-purpose compute family, tailored for compute-heavy parallel workloads that operate with a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance exposes 128 virtual CPUs derived from 64 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include 260 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). There are no GPUs or local storage devices bundled directly on the instance, relying instead on network-attached storage options like Azure Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations highlight robust parallel compute and data delivery metrics. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 107,868.96 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 21,581.0, both placing in the top 10% tier. Instruction sets shine under multi-threaded decompression, reaching 743.41 GB/sec on bzip3, while static web serving throughput hits 173.85 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 516.29 GB/sec. Although single-core throughput remains in the average to strong tiers, multi-core operations perform exceptionally well, supported by dedicated core allocations and extensive instruction acceleration.

From an architectural standpoint, the D128ls_v6 offers strong cost efficiency for high-core processing pipelines that do not require massive per-core memory capacities. By provisioning 2 GB of RAM per vCPU instead of traditional 4 GB or 8 GB allocations, users avoid paying for surplus memory footprint when hosting distributed compute tasks. Tradeoffs include the total absence of local scratch disks and no included public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated storage and networking configuration. It is well matched for Clang software compilation, containerized batch builds, ray tracing, web serving, and CPU-based LLM inference.

The combination of Intel AMX extensions and high core counts makes this instance viable for moderate model inference tasks. Test results demonstrate 307.98 tokens/sec during prompt processing and 44.45 tokens/sec for text generation with 7B parameter models, placing it in the top 10% category among non-GPU configurations. For production use, it provides an efficient operational base for distributed CI/CD pipelines, large scale web application layers, and compute-dense batch jobs.
